status: Closed — sealed publication continuity and fixture parity re-verified 2026-09-02
finding: Committing runner publication outputs can advance HEAD through runner-affecting paths, causing taskflow pre-close to mark the just-published runner-sync receipt as rebuild-required and forcing a second sealed build/publication cycle.
expectedBehavior: Runner-sync publication should converge in one governed transaction, or classify publication-only commits so dist/release output commits do not recursively invalidate their own receipt when the source input tree remains semantically sealed.
evidenceOrRepro: Original incident: ATM-GOV-0252 publication commit advanced HEAD through generated `packages/cli/dist/**`, then pre-close reported `rebuild-required` and required a second build. Current runner-input classification excludes generated `packages/*/dist/**` from both affected-input classification and the sealed input hash. On 2026-09-02, the stale-runner lane regression initially failed because its fixture omitted the now-required `groupManifest.memberTaskIds` and `childAttribution.members`, making the receipt intentionally invalid under the current handoff contract. The fixture now supplies the canonical single-member attribution and the test verifies the ancestor receipt is accepted; true source-input drift, missing attribution, and stale child receipts remain asserted as `rebuild-required` cases.
followUp: Closed. Keep the stale-runner publication continuity regression together with runner publication lifecycle validation.
